name: Bemiparin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Treatment of deep vein thrombosis with or without pulmonary embolism
usual_adult_dose.dose: 115 IU anti-Xa/kg SC once daily for 7 ± 2 days (under 50 kg: 5,000 IU; 50–70 kg: 7,500 IU; 70–100 kg: 10,000 IU; 100–120 kg: 12,500 IU)

usual_adult_dose.indication: DVT with transient risk factors, when oral anticoagulation is contraindicated or unsuitable
usual_adult_dose.dose: 3,500 IU SC once daily, up to 3 months

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Other anticoagulants, aspirin and other antiplatelets, NSAIDs, systemic corticosteroids, dextran

common: Bruising and hematoma at the injection site
serious: Spinal or epidural hematoma with neuraxial anesthesia

contraindications: Current or past immune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Disseminated intravascular coagulation due to heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Central nervous system, eye or ear surgery or injury within 2 months
Lesions prone to bleed (active ulcer, hemorrhagic stroke, aneurysm, brain tumor)
Hypersensitivity to heparins or pork products

pk.half_life_eskd: Anti-Xa exposure significantly higher at CrCl <30 (not quantified)

sources.citation: Laboratorios Farmacéuticos ROVI, S.A. (2023). Hibor 7,500 IU anti-Xa/0.3 mL solución inyectable en jeringas precargadas (bemiparin sodium) [Ficha técnica; text revised May 2023]. Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS), CIMA registration 64165.

revision_log.change: Added contraindication: DIC due to HIT.
3,500 IU regimen scoped to DVT with transient risk factors when oral anticoagulation is unsuitable.
